candidates.changed_node: the 21-day window literal on TS_MIN($low, ...) and TS_MAX($high, ...) -> 63
candidates.rationale: Weakness is regime decay, not noise: IC falls monotonically from +0.0250 (2000) to +0.0010 (2013), and the 19.3-day half-life is just the 21-day lookback, i.e. a one-month reversal whose edge was competed away late in the window. Changed only the range lookback (all three extremum windows, 3 literal edits) to 63 days, making it position-in-the-quarterly-range, a slower state variable with a longer half-life. Archive check: TS_MAX($high,w)-TS_MIN($low,w) is live at w=2, 5, 21, 126, free at 63; TS_MIN($low,63) and $close-TS_MIN($low,63) are not live subtrees.

The 4.3-day IC half-life and the 0.204 turnover both come from the return leg, not the fundamental: a 5-day return sum re-prices weekly while the $roa leg refreshes quarterly, so the factor is being asked to predict far past its own memory. Lengthened only that window to 42 days to match the horizon it is judged on and cut churn. TS_SUM($return,42) only ever appeared inside an evicted member, so the RANK(TS_SUM($return,42)) block is free; 21 was avoided because it converges on the live RANK($roa) - RANK(21-day range position) member.

The corr leg is the weak half: at 15 days it is in the crowded short band, and it is where 2003 (-0.0057) and 2009 (+0.0025) come from, while the range-volume corr pays best at slow windows. Moved only the corr window. 105 rather than 63 because TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, w) is already a live archive subtree at w = 21, 42, 63 and 126, so those windows are instant subtree rejections; 105 is the free slot on the slow side and puts distance between this child and the 42-day corr member it already sits at rho 0.725 against.

Weakest mean IC in the batch (0.00757) with dead years in 2005 (+0.0018) and 2013 (+0.0024): the corr averages 63 days but its x-input is a 5-day within-name percentile that repoints every week, so the correlation is being estimated between a fast noise series and a slow one. Changed only the inner rank window to 21 so both inputs live on comparable timescales; the corr stays at 63, the band where this kernel scores. TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21) is not a live subtree (5 and 10 are taken).

The clip is the weakest component: MAX(delta, 0) ties every falling-leverage name at one rank, so roughly half the cross-section contributes nothing to a multiplicative term that still pays the full 0.200 complexity charge and the one free constant. Dropped the clip and moved the delta to 126 days (3 edits, keeps the term's magnitude). 126 is forced as well as preferred: CS_RANK/CS_ZSCORE/ABS/MAX wrappers around TS_DELTA($leverage,63) are all live 4-node archive blocks, while CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage,126)) is free, and 126 is the only leverage-delta horizon that has worked next to a fundamental level rank.

Worst stability in the batch (0.86): -0.0117 in 2003 and -0.0001 in 2009, both leveraged-junk recovery rallies. That is a fundamental-leg regime problem, not a volume-leg one; $roe is return on equity, so it mechanically rewards leverage and inverts exactly when levered names rally. Swapped that single leaf for $operating_margin, a leverage-free profitability measure and a genuinely different accounting dimension ($roa/$roe swaps do not decorrelate, rho 0.859). The $volume level is left alone: it carries about 0.0088 standalone IC, and within-name volume kernels score an order of magnitude worse.

The binding weakness is crowding, not fit: rho 0.794 against the live leverage member is one hundredth from rejection, and the component they share is the $roe rank. In this archive the fundamental leg dominates rho (14 live members lead with a $roe or $roa rank), so the decorrelating edit has to be the fundamental leaf. Swapped it to $accrual_gap, a different accounting dimension; the only live $accrual_gap spread pairs it with a return-dispersion leg, not a range-volume corr, so the price legs stay distinct.

Weakest kernel here on every axis (mean IC 0.00703, stability 0.86, negative in 2003 and 2013), and the culprit is the 21-day corr window: this kernel is unstable and crowded at short windows and pays at slow ones. Moved only the window. 84 is the nearest free slot to the productive 63-day band, since TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, w) is already a live archive subtree at w = 15, 21, 42, 63 and 126.

Shortest half-life in the batch (4.7 days) on the lowest mean IC (0.00563): a 5-day first difference is a mean-zero noise series, so the corr window is the only component that can give the factor persistence, and at 21 days it does not. Moved only the corr window to 63, the band where this family scores; the short window stays on the volume leg where it belongs. TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,5) is a 3-node block, and no live member holds this corr at 63.

Turnover 0.417 is four times the batch median and the largest charge in this set (0.013), paired with an 8.4-day half-life: the 10-day within-name percentile of the daily range is fully reshuffled every two weeks, so the leg pays costs it does not earn back. Lengthened only that window to 126 so it reads the name's volatility regime rather than last fortnight's noise. TS_RANK($high - $low, w) is live at 10 and 42; 126 is free, and long-window ranks are the second-leg family that has carried accepts here.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Rearranging the operators around two legs does not move rho. MIN(fundamental rank, 1 - price rank) hit 0.806 against the product of the same pair; a fundamental divided by TS_STD($return,42) hit 0.817 against the same rank times a range ratio; and two simultaneous function swaps inside one price leg (TS_MIN to TS_MEAN in the numerator, TS_MEAN to TS_STD in the denominator) still held at 0.833. Change a field or a window, not the functions wrapped around them.
  2. Two legs beat three, on both gates. Bolting a third gated term onto an archived roe-minus-TS_CORR expression still scored rho 0.848, and the one accept whose price leg used three operators over two windows came in at fitness 1.366 while every two-leg accept scored 2.6 to 5.6.
  3. Fundamental acceleration is noise: a 63-day delta minus its own 63-day lag screened at |t| 0.68. The single 63-day TS_DELTA($roa) with no second differencing carried the round's second-best accept at 4.490.
  4. TS_RANK of a price series belongs on the multiplicative side, not in a rank spread. Subtracted from a fundamental rank at 42 days it screened at |t| 0.63; multiplied against a fundamental z-score at 168 days it scored 4.490.
  5. The range-vs-volume correlation band has moved to 63 days: TS_CORR(TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 5), $high - $low, 63) scored 5.235 and a bare 63-day TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low) leg scored 4.609, while the same kernel at 21 days was rejected at rho 0.817. Keep the corr window at 63 and put any short window on the volume leg, not on the corr.
  6. Wrapping or re-normalising the volume leg does not decorrelate a corr that reuses an archived window: TS_RANK($volume, 63) inside a 21-day corr hit rho 0.817, and swapping $dollar_volume / $open for $dollar_volume / TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) hit rho 0.917. Move the corr window instead.
  7. Dividing a fundamental by anything screens weakly. Fundamental-over-fundamental was 0 for 4 ($eps/$book_per_share 0.12, $accrual_gap/$asset_turnover 0.44, TS_DELTA($eps,63)/$book_per_share 0.10, TS_DELTA($book_per_share,63)/$book_per_share 0.63), and fundamental-over-price-level was the weakest surviving family (best accept 0.745, rejects at 0.51 and 0.66). Cross the fundamental with a price/volume leg instead of scaling it.
  8. Normalise ranges and vols by TS_MEAN or TS_SUM of $high - $low, never by TS_MAX($high, w) - TS_MIN($low, w) or a TS_MIN/TS_MIN ratio: the extremum denominators were 0 for 3 at |t| 0.43-0.58, while the averaged-range denominators scored 3.205 and 3.178.
  9. TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) cannot be the cross-sectional driver: three rejects at |t| 0.40-0.68 when it led the expression. It worked only at 126 days as the subtracted modifier next to a fundamental level rank (CS_RANK($roe) form, 4.051).
  10. Bare short-window within-name rank legs are dead on the cheap screen: TS_RANK($volume, 3) 0.51, TS_RANK($open - $low, 5) 0.66, TS_ARGMIN($low, 10) 0.40, TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 21) - TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 5) 0.79. Second legs that carried accepts were volatility/range ratios or long-window ranks (TS_RANK($close, 126), TS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 5), 42)).
  11. Sign and clip reductions destroy the second leg: SIGN(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) screened at 0.40 and TS_SUM(MIN($return, 0), 21) at 0.02, the worst of the round. Keep the magnitude of the leg.
  12. $roa's bare rank is already in the archive and dominates rho, so multiplying CS_RANK($roa) by a mild price-vol ratio still collided at 0.930. Reserve $roa and $roe for difference forms and use $accrual_gap, $asset_turnover or $operating_margin * $asset_turnover as the fundamental leg of a product.
